findings_qualitative.value: Two symmetric trailing spiral arms with low optical depth trace midplane density/temperature enhancements; a low-contrast gap lies at ~70 AU.

evidence.quote: these results imply that NW and SE are tracing density and/or temperature enhancements at the disk midplane

claims.hypothesis: Spiral arms in the Elias 2-27 disk trace midplane spiral density waves
claims.experiment: 1.3 mm ALMA imaging, polar projection, ring/spiral fitting, optical depth modeling
claims.result: Two symmetric arms with contrast 1.3-2.5, optically thin (tau 0.02-0.1)
claims.finding: Arms trace spiral density waves in the midplane

evidence.quote: We conclude that instead of tracing material arms, the NW and SE spiral structures trace density and temperature enhancements due to spiral density waves

claims.hypothesis: Spirals are driven by gravitational instability alone
claims.experiment: Toomre Q and disk-to-star mass ratio comparison
claims.result: Q well in stable regime; Mdisk/Mstar at most ~0.3

evidence.quote: even in the most optimistic case the disk-to-star mass ratio is $M_{disk}$/$M_{star} \approx 0.3$, limiting the possibility of GI acting alone

claims.hypothesis: The 70 AU gap results from grain growth

evidence.quote: Thus, the gap at 70 AU likely traces a decrement in density of material rather than a pure grain growth effect.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Planet-disk interaction alone rejected as it struggles to produce symmetric arms of equal contrast; GI alone and PDI+GI also disfavored

evidence.quote: Those models often struggle to produce the symmetric spiral pattern observed in the Elias 2-27 disk

limitations_admitted.value: Contrast values are lower limits because of possible beam dilution and higher optical depth.

evidence.quote: Thus, the contrast values measured for NW and SE are lower limits.
